minutes.headline: Capital committee heard fire and police capital plans and questioned a third ambulance; only adjournment was voted.
minutes.summary: After a member raised a Town Meeting complaint that capital procedures are unfair to the schools, the committee heard the new fire chief's ten-year plan and the police chief's vehicle and equipment plan. Discussion centred on adding a third ambulance, moving tasers into the operating budget, and the special vehicle stabilization fund. No substantive votes were taken.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee heard the fire and police capital plans and took no votes other than adjournment.
The fire chief's ten-year plan drew discussion of adding a third ambulance as a mechanical spare, with a member arguing it must be justified by billing revenue.
Members and the chief suggested the special vehicle stabilization fund might cover the rescue pumper and the ambulance.
On police items, members favoured putting tasers in the operating budget rather than a multi-year payment plan, and the chief expects FY27 cruisers to come in under the approved number.
A member raised a complaint that capital procedures are unfair to the schools; it would become a future agenda item if taken up.

why_it_matters: Ambulances, fire trucks, cruisers and equipment are paid through the capital plan, so choices about the stabilization fund, the operating budget or grants affect what appears on future Town Meeting warrants and tax bills.
Moving tasers into the operating budget would shift a recurring cost from the capital plan to the yearly operating budget, which is mostly paid by taxes.
